ch31.f.d.R: Resistance $R$ of the circuit; 0 gives an undamped LC oscillation
ch31.f.d.spring: Show a block on a spring whose displacement $x$ is proportional to the charge $q$
ch31.f.goal.exchange: LC oscillation: energy passes back and forth between the electric field of the capacitor and the magnetic field of the inductor; the total stays constant
ch31.f.goal.damp: With resistance, energy leaves as heat and the amplitude decays (damped oscillation)
ch31.f.obs.exchange: When $q$ is largest, $i = 0$ and all the energy is $U_E$; when $q = 0$, $\lvert i\rvert$ is largest and all the energy is $U_B$
ch31.f.obs.phase: $i(t)$ runs a quarter period ahead of $q(t)$: $i = dq/dt$
ch31.f.obs.spring: Spring analogue: $q \leftrightarrow x$, $i \leftrightarrow v$, $L \leftrightarrow m$, $1/C \leftrightarrow k$, so the same differential equation gives the same motion
ch31.f.obs.damp: 5 Ω and 20 Ω: the oscillation decays as $e^{-Rt/2L}$ and the total energy $U$ drops
ch31.f.obs.over: 100 Ω ($R > 2\sqrt{L/C}$): the charge returns to 0 without oscillating (overdamped)
ch31.f.assume: Initial capacitor voltage 10 V, initial current 0. Ideal components (no coil resistance, no radiation). Time runs slowed down, in ms
ch31.a.d.ratio: Angular frequency $\omega_d$ of the emf as a multiple of the natural frequency $\omega_0 = 1/\sqrt{LC}$
ch31.a.d.mode: Slope of $i(t)$ ($v_L \propto di/dt$) or area under it ($v_C \propto \int i\,dt$)
ch31.a.d.R: Resistance $R$ of the circuit; smaller R gives a sharper resonance curve
ch31.a.goal.phase: Why the phases differ: $v_R = iR$ is in phase with $i$, $v_L = L\,di/dt$ leads by $90^\circ$, $v_C = q/C$ lags by $90^\circ$
ch31.a.goal.res: Resonance: at $\omega_d = \omega_0$, $v_L + v_C = 0$, the impedance is smallest ($Z = R$) and the current largest
ch31.a.obs.R: $v_R$ (purple) peaks and crosses zero together with $i$
ch31.a.obs.L: Slope view: $v_L$ peaks where $i$ is steepest (crossing zero), so $v_L$ leads $i$ by a quarter period
ch31.a.obs.C: Area view: the area under $i$ is the charge $\Delta q$ delivered, and it keeps building until $i$ reaches 0, so $v_C$ peaks a quarter period later (charge takes time to build up)
ch31.a.obs.phasor: Phasors all rotate at the same rate; their projections on the vertical axis (dots) are the instantaneous values. $\vec V_L$ and $\vec V_C$ are perpendicular to $\vec I$ and opposite to each other
ch31.a.obs.res: Driving ratio 1: $V_L = V_C$ cancel, $\mathcal{E}$ and $i$ are in phase ($\phi = 0$); $V_L$ and $V_C$ can exceed $\mathcal{E}_m$
ch31.a.obs.sweep: Changing the driving frequency moves the point along the resonance curve on the right. $\omega_d < \omega_0$: capacitive ($\phi < 0$); $\omega_d > \omega_0$: inductive ($\phi > 0$)
ch31.a.assume: Steady state (no transient), $L$ = 10 mH, $C$ = 10 μF ($\omega_0$ = 3162 rad/s), $\mathcal{E}_m$ = 10 V. The current phasor shows direction only, not length. One driving period plays in 2.5 s
